doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: First seeing and getting to know Joe Williams
summary: He first saw Williams with the Basie band at Birdland and later spent a night with him in a Chicago club.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Let’s talk about Joe for a bit.
Well let’s talk about Joe Williams.
When was the first time that you actually got to know him?

How about the first time I saw him? I was back here on a shipbuilding expedition with my chief engineer and the two of us went to Birdland. And we had a table about so big in the front row, of the Basie band. I didn’t know Joe Williams from a hill of beans. And we were sitting there talking very seriously about a problem. And all of a sudden I looked down and there were the biggest feet I’ve ever seen in my life. Huge feet. And I looked up and up and up and up, and here’s this big, ugly, black man. And it was Joe. And he started to sing. And we thought that was pretty good. And then I started collecting his records after that. This was in the 50s, when he first sprang up with the Basie band, before he went on his own. And as you may notice from the collection we have all of Joe’s records, all that we know of anyway. And I was very enamored of his talent. Still am. I believe that he never received the recognition he should have. That as a blues singer he was terrific but on a ballad he was fantastic. He’s just got a beautiful voice. And a couple of his songs, a couple of his recordings, I have used to woo my wife sitting over there. So it’s very dear to me. And I guess the next time I really saw him and got to know him, I was in Chicago. And it was a snowy night and I was on my way from the Blackstone Hotel to the one that has the pump room across town. Anyway, we’re in a cab driving down Rush Street and there is a place called New Orleans or something like that, it’s a New Orleans type name, and it had big letters, Joe Williams. I says stop the cab. And I got out and I went in. And I sat in the front row and we started talking between sets. And finally he said well come on back. So I went in the back room and sat there all night. And we talked about everything in the world. Race relations, you name it. And became very close. And went from there.
